With less than four years to implement the 2030 agenda, only 36% of the Sustainable Development Goals are on track or or showing moderate progress.
While developing countries face an annual financing gap exceeding US $4 trillion.
The civil commitment must now be implemented through greater affordable, long term and concessional finance.
Timely development oriented debt treatment and a more effective channelling of special drawing rights development cannot flourish when its financing is prohibitively expensive.
Reform must decisively address Africa's excessive risk premiums and borrowing costs.

The need to strengthen the voice of developing countries in global financing institutions cap illicit financial flows and tax abuse, as well as secure fair returns from natural resources cannot be over emphasized.

Zimbabwe is continuously strengthening its capacity to mobilise domestic resources, enhance public financial management and foster a favourable environment for productive investment and our National Vision 2030.
We are strengthening the important linkage between mining and agriculture, which is driving growth in Zimbabwe's manufacturing sector.
Zimbabwe is indeed open for business.
We are also pursuing food and nutrition, security and the climate smart agriculture.
My government is leaving no one and no place behind.
Through our rural industrialisation agenda and the Invest Rural policy, we are directing investment towards rural infrastructure, manufacturing hubs and agro processing facilities.
More women and youth continue to enter value chain industries for both our local and regional markets.
As droughts, floods and declining productivity threaten water, food and energy security.

Developed countries are called upon to honour their climate finance commitments in line with common but differentiated responsibilities Mr. president, Zimbabwe welcomes the recommendations of the Secretary-General's Panel on Critical Energy Transition Minerals and the country's support mechanism.

This has seen us dispatch the first export of locally produced lithium sulfate during the second quarter of the year, demonstrating that remaining value added resource retaining value at the source is possible for shared prosperity.
Harnessing emerging technologies for national development is a key priority for our industrialisation agenda.
Zimbabwe's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026 to 2030 promotes human centred, ethical and responsible innovation.
Artificial intelligence must narrow development gaps while its military use, including in nuclear command and control, must remain subject to human judgment, accountability and international law.
Regrettably, however, my country's national development initiatives have continued to be undermined by unilateral coercive measures imposed by some Western countries.
We call for their immediate and unconditional removal.
I reiterate Zimbabwe is a friend to all and an enemy to none unless you choose to be an enemy.

Mr. president, Zimbabwe supports U.N. reforms that reduce duplication, improve coordination, modernize systems and strengthen filled implementation.
At this juncture of global development, the success of reforms should be reflected by the conflicts prevented development advanced, assistance delivered, and communities strengthened.
The selection of the next Secretary-General, therefore, comes at a defining moment.
The next holder of the office should be an impartial custodian of the charter.
An independent voice for peace, a bridge builder among member states, and an advocate for those whose voices seldom reach these halls.
The process should be transparent, inclusive and guided by merit.
Equitable geographical representation and gender equality.
Above all, the next Secretary-General must bring the United Nations closer to the people.
The charter begins with we, the peoples of the United Nations.

In conclusion, Zimbabwe will assume its role in the Security Council.
Mindful that membership is not a badge of honor, but a commitment to serve the comity of nations.

We will serve with balance and integrity, defend the sovereign equality of states, advance Africa's priorities and work constructively with all regions Let this 81st decision be recorded as the session that closed the gap between the promises of the charter and the realities of the daily life, Zimbabwe is ready to play its part in building the future we all want.
